fixed.blackTriangle: ▼ This medicinal product is subject to additional monitoring in Australia. This will allow quick identification of new safety information. Healthcare professionals are asked to report any suspected adverse events at www.tga.gov.au/reporting-problems.

blocks.text: Lumiravostat
Each film-coated tablet contains 10 mg or 25 mg of lumiravostat. For the full list of excipients, see Section 6.1 List of excipients.
10 mg: white, round, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "10" on the other.
25 mg: yellow, oval, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "25" on the other.
OSTREVIA is indicated for the treatment of adults with moderate to severe chronic hand eczema that has not responded adequately to potent topical corticosteroids, or when these are not advisable.
The recommended dose is 10 mg once daily, with or without food. The dose may be increased to 25 mg once daily if the response is inadequate after 12 weeks.
Moderate hepatic impairment: 10 mg once daily. Severe hepatic impairment: not recommended.
With strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (for example ketoconazole or clarithromycin): 10 mg once daily.
Hypersensitivity to lumiravostat or any excipient. Active tuberculosis or active serious infection. Pregnancy (Category D, fictional).

subs.title: Special warnings and precautions for use

blocks.text: Serious infections, including tuberculosis, pneumonia, cellulitis and herpes zoster, have been reported, some leading to hospitalization or death. Screen patients for latent tuberculosis before starting treatment and treat it first. Interrupt treatment if a serious infection develops.
Malignancy, including lymphoma and non-melanoma skin cancer, has been reported. Consider the risks and benefits before starting treatment in patients with a known malignancy.
Venous thromboembolism, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, has been reported. Use with caution in patients with risk factors and stop treatment if it occurs.
Monitor lymphocyte and neutrophil counts, haemoglobin and liver enzymes at baseline, at 4 weeks and every 3 months.

subs.title: Interactions with other medicines and other forms of interactions

blocks.text: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase lumiravostat exposure (use 10 mg once daily). Strong CYP3A4 inducers, such as rifampicin, reduce exposure; avoid concomitant use.

Lumiravostat caused embryo-fetal toxicity in rats and rabbits. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 weeks after the last dose.
It is not known whether lumiravostat passes into human milk. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 4 days after the last dose.

subs.title: Effects on ability to drive and use machines

blocks.text: OSTREVIA has no or negligible influence on the ability to drive and use machines.

pneumonia, cellulitis, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism

blocks.text: Reporting suspected adverse effects: Reporting suspected adverse reactions after registration of the medicinal product is important. It allows continued monitoring of the benefit-risk balance of the medicinal product. Healthcare professionals are asked to report any suspected adverse reactions at www.tga.gov.au/reporting-problems.
There is no specific antidote. Monitor the patient for signs of adverse reactions and give supportive treatment. Lumiravostat is not removed by haemodialysis to a meaningful extent.
For information on the management of overdose, contact the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26 (Australia).
Lumiravostat is a reversible inhibitor of the fictional STRK1 kinase, which signals downstream of several cytokines involved in skin inflammation.
Dose-dependent reductions in markers of skin inflammation were seen within 2 weeks.

Clinical trials: In two 16-week placebo-controlled studies (fictional HANDS-1 and HANDS-2, 1,210 adults), 38% of patients on lumiravostat 25 mg and 31% on 10 mg reached clear or almost clear hands, against 12% on placebo.
Peak plasma concentrations are reached 1 to 2 hours after a dose. The half-life is about 16 hours. Lumiravostat is metabolised mainly by CYP3A4.
Lumiravostat was not genotoxic. Embryo-fetal toxicity was seen in rats and rabbits at exposures close to the human exposure at 25 mg.
Microcrystalline cellulose, mannitol, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate; film coat: hypromellose, titanium dioxide, macrogol (25 mg tablets also iron oxide yellow).
Incompatibilities were either not assessed or not identified as part of the registration of this medicine.
In Australia, information on the shelf life can be found on the public summary of the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG). The expiry date can be found on the packaging.
Store below 30°C. Store in the original package.
Aluminium/aluminium blister packs of 28 tablets.
In Australia, any unused medicine or waste material should be disposed of by taking it to your local pharmacy.
Chemical structure: fictional. CAS number: not applicable (fictional substance).

items: 1. Why am I using OSTREVIA? It contains lumiravostat and is used to treat long-lasting hand eczema in adults.
2. What should I know before I use OSTREVIA? Do not use it if you are allergic to it, have an active serious infection or tuberculosis, or are pregnant.
3. What if I am taking other medicines? Some medicines may interfere with OSTREVIA.
4. How do I use OSTREVIA? Take one tablet once a day.
5. What should I know while using OSTREVIA? Tell your doctor straight away if you have signs of infection.
6. Are there any side effects? Common side effects include cold symptoms, headache and acne. Serious side effects include infections and blood clots.

blocks.text: OSTREVIA contains the active ingredient lumiravostat. It calms the immune activity that causes long-lasting hand eczema when creams have not worked well enough.

sections.title: What should I know before I use OSTREVIA?

blocks.text: Do not use OSTREVIA if you are allergic to lumiravostat or any of the ingredients listed at the end of this leaflet, if you have tuberculosis or another serious infection, or if you are pregnant.
Check with your doctor if you have had tuberculosis, cancer or blood clots, or have liver problems.

sections.title: What if I am taking other medicines?

blocks.text: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking any other medicines, including any medicines, vitamins or supplements that you buy without a prescription. Some antifungals, antibiotics and St John’s wort may interfere with OSTREVIA.
Take one tablet once a day, with or without food. Swallow it whole with water. If you forget a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless the next dose is due within 12 hours.

sections.title: What should I know while using OSTREVIA?

rows: Tell your doctor straight away if you have a fever, cough or a painful swollen leg.
Do not stop taking it or change the dose without checking with your doctor.
Store below 30°C in the original pack.

blocks.text: All medicines can have side effects. If you do experience any side effects, most of them are minor and temporary.

rows: Speak to your doctor if you have any of these less serious side effects and they worry you.
Fever, cough, painful blistering rash; pain or swelling in a leg, chest pain or sudden breathlessness
Call your doctor straight away, or go straight to the Emergency Department at your nearest hospital if you notice any of these serious side effects.

blocks.text: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you notice anything else that may be making you feel unwell. Other side effects not listed here may occur in some people.

Reporting side effects: After you have received medical advice for any side effects you experience, you can report side effects to the Therapeutic Goods Administration online at www.tga.gov.au/reporting-problems.
This medicine is only available with a doctor’s prescription.

What OSTREVIA contains: lumiravostat 10 mg or 25 mg; inactive ingredients microcrystalline cellulose, mannitol, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate; film coat: hypromellose, titanium dioxide, macrogol (25 mg tablets also iron oxide yellow). Do not take this medicine if you are allergic to any of these ingredients.

What OSTREVIA looks like: 10 mg: white, round, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "10" on the other. 25 mg: yellow, oval, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "25" on the other. (AUST R 999101, AUST R 999102, fictional).
Who distributes OSTREVIA: Halcyon Ridge Pharmaceuticals Australia Pty Ltd, Level 5, 10 Example Street, Fictionville NSW 2000.
